sn12.59:1.2: “Bhikkhus, when one dwells contemplating gratification in things that can fetter, there is a descent of consciousness.
sn12.59:1.3: With consciousness as condition, name-and-form comes to be….
sn12.59:1.4: Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.
sn12.59:2.1: “Suppose, bhikkhus, there was a great tree,
sn12.59:2.2: and all its roots going downwards and across would send the sap upwards. Sustained by that sap, nourished by it, that great tree would stand for a very long time.
sn12.59:2.3: So too, when one lives contemplating gratification in things that can fetter, there is a descent of consciousness…. Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.
sn12.59:3.1: “When, bhikkhus, one dwells contemplating danger in things that can fetter, there is no descent of consciousness.
sn12.59:3.2: With the cessation of consciousness comes cessation of name-and-form….
sn12.59:3.3: Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.
sn12.59:4.1: “Suppose, bhikkhus, there was a great tree.
sn12.59:4.2: Then a man would come along bringing a shovel and a basket.
sn12.59:4.3: He would cut down the tree at its foot … he would winnow the ashes in a strong wind or let them be carried away by the swift current of a river. Thus that great tree would be cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated so that it is no more subject to future arising.
sn12.59:4.4: “So too, bhikkhus, when one dwells contemplating danger in things that can fetter, there is no descent of consciousness….
sn12.59:4.6: Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”
